summary: Source-anchored research for simulateTransaction before send. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Simulation errors leave no on-chain record. Metaplex tells developers to send with `skipPreflight: true` when they need a failing transaction recorded on chain, with its logs visible in an explorer. The failed transaction still pays its fee, so use this for debugging, not as a default. (medium confidence)

A simulation reflects one RPC node's view. If the node lags, a dependent simulation can fail with missing-account errors because it has not seen a just-confirmed transaction. The program-metadata CU estimator hit this on a hosted devnet RPC, and the suggested fix is to pass the confirmation slot as minContextSlot to simulateTransaction and to retry such simulations. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-11)

Agave's simulate path builds its batch with prepare_unlocked_batch_from_single_tx ('without locking accounts') and never commits the result. A passing simulation therefore says nothing about write-lock contention with other transactions or about scheduler and block-limit behavior. That consequence is an inference from the code; no doc states it. (low confidence)

A transaction that fails on chain still costs the fee. Solana's fee docs say the total fee (5,000 lamports per signature plus the priority fee) is deducted before execution and is charged whether the transaction succeeds or fails. A failure caught by preflight costs nothing, because the node rejects it before forwarding. With skipPreflight true, every deterministic error that preflight would have caught is paid for if the transaction lands. The retry guide titles this 'The Cost of Skipping Preflight'. (high confidence)

Aggregators can run the simulation for you. Jupiter's v6 /swap parameter dynamicComputeUnitLimit does a swap simulation to set the compute-unit limit and, per its own spec, 'will increase latency slightly since there will be one extra RPC call to simulate this'. QuickNode's Jupiter guide says the API returns a simulated transaction, so skipPreflight can be set true. Jupiter's current docs page says the Metis Swap API is superseded by Swap V2, so these parameter docs may be stale. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

The default simulation commitment is finalized. Helius says a blockhash fetched at confirmed can look too new to an RPC that validates against finalized, so simulateTransaction should be called with replaceRecentBlockhash set, and preflightCommitment should match the commitment used to fetch the blockhash. (medium confidence)

Triton's `/sendtx` endpoint always submits without a preflight simulation and does not support `skipPreflight: false`, so a bot that sends through it must run `simulateTransaction` through the normal RPC interface first. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

A reconstructed bot case from a vendor-adjacent post says failures first read as 'slippage exceeded' were stale state: the shared RPC ran 2-3 slots behind and the simulation at submit time used stale data. The post calls itself a composite case, so use it only as illustration. (low confidence)
Simulating from a fee payer that holds no SOL returns 'Attempt to debit an account but found no record of a prior credit.'; Metaplex says this means the account has no SOL. (low confidence)

A bot can read the effect of a transaction without landing it. The accounts config returns post-simulation account data for chosen addresses, and the result includes preBalances, postBalances, preTokenBalances and postTokenBalances, from which a net lamport or token change can be computed. These values describe only the simulation bank's state at the chosen commitment. (medium confidence)
